title.en: Psychedelia in Los Angeles and elsewhere
title.zh: 洛杉矶及其他地方的迷幻音乐

summary.en: From the 1960s the music industry accelerated its shift from New York to Los Angeles; the chief L.A. psychedelic representative is the Doors.
summary.zh: 60年代开始，音乐产业从纽约加速向洛杉矶转移，洛杉矶迷幻音乐代表当属The Doors。

body.zh:
60年代开始，音乐产业从纽约加速向洛杉矶转移，洛杉矶迷幻音乐代表当属The Doors。

我们已经花了很多时间讨论旧金山和伦敦的迷幻音乐，你们或许认为只有这两个地方真正出现了迷幻音乐。的确，我们所谈论的迷幻亚文化在这两个地方最为成熟也最为重要。但在这段时期，即60年代的早期、中期、再到晚期，音乐产业开始加速向洛杉矶转移。音乐产业从纽约移到洛杉矶有各种重要的原因，其中之一是洛杉矶好莱坞有许多来自电影产业的先进设备。电视产业也加速搬到了洛杉矶，因此唱片公司得到了很多与电视电影合作的机会。电影公司要么是本地企业，要么在那里有分支机构。因此许多音乐家都从东海岸搬到了西海岸，厂牌也是这样，于是在1965、1966、1967年洛杉矶出现了一些新事物。

我们曾讲过美国对于英伦入侵的回应，我们要说的第一个重要的乐队，就是谈及洛杉矶和迷幻音乐时必提的The Doors。The Doors和其他迷幻乐队的不同之处在于，一般来说迷幻音乐包含乌托邦式的、权力归花 (flower power) 之类的正能量。（注：Flower power是在1960年代末至1970年代初的一句口号，标志着消极抵抗和非暴力思想。）因此支持LSD最为理想主义的原因是，它能带来更高层次的意识觉悟，这是一件让人愉快的事，不是吗？它是人心之所向。再次声明，我并不主张使用LSD，我只是在阐述一个支持迷幻药的原因。但正如Jim Morrison所说，如果你陷入了幻境，那里可能是天堂，也可能是地狱。所以就让他人来谈论天堂吧，我来思索地狱。从很多方面来说，Jim Morrison对于迷幻音乐的看法要更加阴暗。它与许多精神层面上的东西有关，我们一般很少讨论。Jim Morrison的歌词也十分有内涵。尽管作为歌手，他不会演奏乐器，也不会弹吉他和弦，但他会在脑中形成旋律并唱出来，由其他乐队成员来确定他在唱什么，旋律由哪些音符组成，该用什么和弦来为它伴奏，节奏应该是什么样的。所以从很多方面来说，The Doors是一个非常民主的乐队，很多情况下，他们四人平分写歌所得的版税。

他们的第一张专辑《The Doors》在1967年1月发行，就在《Sgt. Pepper》之前，实际上它比《Penny Lane》和《Strawberry Fields》这两首歌发行得还要早。因此，当我们考虑到他们的成就时，与The Beatles和The Beach Boys这类乐队相比，他们更加领先且相对独立。The Doors 比跟随他们的一些乐队资历要老一点，和The Beatles、The Rolling Stones几乎处在同一时代。他们主要受到50年代后期的rock and roll以及60年代初期爵士音乐的影响，不同于其他乐队，他们受The Beatles及英伦入侵的影响较少。他们的远见在于Jim Morrison，他是个诗人，大学毕业且涉猎过大量文学作品。至于乐队其他人，Ray Manzarek略微年长，有许多俱乐部演出经验；Robert Krieger是一位十分有才华的歌曲创作者，John Densmore是个爵士风格的鼓手。他们聚在一起为乐队取名The Doors，取自阿道司·赫胥黎所写的一本关于麦斯卡林（一种迷幻药）使用的书《The Doors of perception》。而赫胥黎的灵感则来自William Blake的诗，其中提到“the Doors of Perception”。所以可见，这些联系可以追溯到19世纪的文学和唯灵论（spiritualism）。因此The Doors的第一张专辑《The Doors》的第一首歌即《Break On Through (To The Other Side)》，将通向另一个世界的知觉之门（the Doors of Perception）这个理念表达的十分清楚，但另一个世界也许并不是个好地方。此时，专辑中第一首单曲《Break On Through》的成绩并不理想。因此他们又用了Robby Krieger写的歌《Light My Fire》，这首歌起初有七分钟长，他们砍掉了歌曲中间的全部solo，将它作为AM电台单曲发布，这首歌在榜单上登顶。拥有一首冠军单曲对于The Doors是非常重要的，这也是他们所在厂牌Elektra Records的历史最佳成绩。所以一定程度上，他们也带动了Elektra唱片公司的发展。但在专辑的结尾，你可以从《The End》中听到许多阴暗的内容，Jim Morrison采用了部落歌谣式的手法，整首歌几乎令人感到恐惧：他于深夜在房间里行走，来到父亲面前说“我想杀了你”，接着又对母亲说 “我想和你在一起”，这已经是很文雅的说法了，但他的原话一点也不含蓄，而是一种复杂饥渴的想要和母亲结婚的情绪，非常阴暗可怕。当他们现场演唱这首歌时，人们都震惊了。Jim Morrison通过使人们面对这样的阴暗面，将人们从自我满足中震醒。因此，这是一种非常阴暗的迷幻音乐。The Doors发行了六张专辑，最后一张是《L.A woman》，在1971年排名第九。讽刺的是，这张专辑被认为是The Doors的回归专辑，我说它讽刺是因为1971年7月Jim Morrison在巴黎死于心脏衰竭，成为继Jimi Hendricks和Janis Joplin之后第三个去世的摇滚巨星。

The Doors一定程度上代表了洛杉矶的迷幻音乐，但它并不是在洛杉矶的唯一乐队。我们之前曾提过几次Arthur Lee以及他的乐队Love，事实上Love比The Doors更早与Elektra唱片公司签约。他们本也能取得The Doors那样的成功，但Arthur Lee不愿意坐飞机，这就代表着他们无法巡演。而如果不巡演，那么你的音乐只能在洛杉矶流行。我是说，在洛杉矶，他们是非常成功的，与他们相比，The Doors就显得渺小了。The Doors非常幸运能为Love的演唱会开场，Arthur Lee认为他们挺棒的，于是他将乐队推荐给Jac Holzman，自己也签了Elektra唱片公司，结果The Doors脱颖而出而Love走向平凡。他们有一首相对热门的单曲《My Little Red Book》，在1966年排52名，我们之前在谈论Pink Floyd时曾说过这首歌。他们在1967年发行的第三张专辑《Forever Changes》一直被摇滚乐评论家认为是一张伟大的、被忽视的迷幻摇滚专辑。或许你也想听听《Forever Changes》，看看这是不是被忽视的经典。

另一个来自西海岸的乐队Iron Butterfly以重型摇滚为特色，他们来自圣地亚哥。他们的第二张专辑最为成功，叫作《In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida》，发行于1968年夏天。当然，同名歌曲一开始被叫作《In a Garden of Eden》，他们想到可以改为 “In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida”。在《辛普森一家（the Simpsons）》某一集里，它又一次被叫作《In the Garden of Eden》，用谷歌搜索Simpsons In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida可以看到这个极好的小插曲介绍。（注：在剧集中，Bart在教堂中将这首歌作为赞美诗《In the Garden of Eden》散发，作曲家归功于Iron Butterfly。）无论如何，《In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida》同名歌曲有17分钟长，每个乐队成员都solo了一段，这首歌是重曲调的，所有的solo都非常精湛，也有点迷幻风格。

另一个我们需要提到的乐队Vanilla Fudge来自于东海岸，我们称之为“迷幻乐交响版”。他们十分擅长把一首短小的歌变成一场迷幻摇滚之旅，其中最著名的一首是1967年的《You Keep Me Hangin' On》，这首歌在一年前还只是首时长仅两分钟的Holland–Dozier–Holland为The Supremes创作的热单。它原本只有两分钟，但在Vanilla Fudge改编后，它变成了一首运用了印度西塔琴的五分钟歌曲，我经常让学生听完前几分钟后猜猜歌曲的走向，大部分人都猜不到。像这样把短小的歌曲改编成大型迷幻交响乐的想法，是Vanilla Fudge的专长。他们有一张1968年的专辑《The Beat Goes On》，它的制作人Shadow Martin与Brill Building以及女子组合都有很深的渊源。乐队对于这个专辑并不满意，但其中他们引用了Sonny & Cher的歌《The Beat Goes On》作为动机，在专辑中反复出现、贯穿始终。改编的歌曲可以上溯到整个音乐史，从18世纪、19世纪，直到20世纪，还包括The Beatles的歌，组成了一张野心极大的概念专辑。我认为Vanilla Fudge的改编，为之后的前卫摇滚做出了很大的贡献，其本质是将短小的歌曲转变为长篇巨作。

既然说到了这段时期，我们应该谈谈纽约北部和Bob Dylan。Bob Dylan在1966年的摩托车事故后，便在纽约州的伍德斯托克隐居，你们可能不知道这个地方在哪儿，它在纽约市北部约几小时路程的地方。但它确实被认为是在纽约州郊区，那里给人以乡村朴实的感觉，在那儿Bob Dylan和一个乐队The Band一起录制唱片。他们一开始取名为The Hawks，以此向加拿大歌手Ronnie Hawkins致敬，除了Levon Helm以外其他乐队成员都是加拿大人。他们曾跟随Bob Dylan在65、66年做世界巡演，他们早就在一起合作了。因此当Bob Dylan在伍德斯托克隐居时，他与这些人录了许多作品，这些作品在1975年的《The Basement Tapes》中发布。就在这段时间，两张重要的唱片发行了，一张来自Bob Dylan，另一张来自The Band，这两张唱片不仅定义了Americana运动，对此后乡村摇滚（country rock）的崛起也至关重要。它们都在1968年发行，Bob Dylan的《John Wesley Harding》在专辑榜上排行第二，The Band的《Music From Big Pink》尽管只排在了第三十位，但它被认为是一张非常有影响力的唱片。

到这里，我们就说完了洛杉矶和其他地区的音乐发展。下节课，我们会讨论音乐节，这意味着在1967年夏季迷幻音乐风靡全国之后，嬉皮席卷全国，这些都会在本章的最后一节课里谈到。
body.en:
From the 1960s the music industry accelerated its shift from New York to Los Angeles; the chief L.A. psychedelic representative is the Doors.

We have spent much time on San Francisco and London psychedelia; you might think only those two places truly had it. Indeed the psychedelic subcultures we discuss were most mature and important there. But in this period—early, mid, and late 1960s—the industry accelerated its move to Los Angeles. Reasons for the shift from New York to L.A. include Hollywood’s advanced film equipment. Television also moved west, so labels got more film and TV work. Film companies were local or had branches there. Many musicians moved from East Coast to West; so did labels. In 1965–67 new things appeared in Los Angeles.

We covered America’s reply to the British Invasion; the first important band we name for L.A. and psychedelia is the Doors. They differ from other psychedelic bands: generally psychedelic music carried utopian, flower-power positive energy. (Note: “flower power” was a late-1960s–early-1970s slogan for passive resistance and nonviolence.) So the most idealistic case for LSD was higher consciousness—pleasant, desirable, right? Again: I do not advocate LSD; I am stating one argument for it. But as Jim Morrison put it, if you break into another realm it might be heaven or hell. Let others talk about heaven; he would think about hell. In many ways Morrison’s take on psychedelic music was darker. It tied to spiritual matters we rarely discuss. His lyrics were also substantial. As a singer he did not play instruments or guitar chords, but he formed melodies in his head and sang them; the others figured out what he was singing, which notes, what chords, what rhythm. So in many ways the Doors were a very democratic band; often they split songwriting royalties four ways.

Their first album, The Doors, came out in January 1967—before Sgt. Pepper, actually before “Penny Lane” and “Strawberry Fields Forever.” So relative to the Beatles and Beach Boys they were ahead and relatively independent. They were a bit senior to some bands that followed them, nearly of the same generation as the Beatles and Stones. Main influences: late-1950s rock and roll and early-1960s jazz; unlike others, less shaped by the Beatles and the Invasion. Vision came from Morrison—a poet, college-educated, widely read. Ray Manzarek was a bit older, with much club experience; Robby Krieger a gifted songwriter; John Densmore a jazz-leaning drummer. They named the band the Doors after Huxley’s book on mescaline, The Doors of Perception. Huxley took the phrase from William Blake’s poetry about the doors of perception. So the links reach back to nineteenth-century literature and spiritualism. The album’s first song, “Break On Through (To the Other Side),” states the doors-of-perception idea clearly—but the other side may not be a good place. That first single did not do well. So they used Robby Krieger’s “Light My Fire,” originally about seven minutes; they cut the middle solos for an AM single, and it went to No. 1. A chart-topper mattered for the Doors and was Elektra Records’ best result to then; to a degree they helped grow Elektra. But at the album’s end, “The End” holds much darkness: Morrison in tribal-chant mode, almost frightening—walking at night, telling his father “I want to kill you,” then his mother “I want to be with you”—that is the polite version; the original is blunt, a complex hungry wish to marry the mother, very dark. Live, people were shocked. By confronting that darkness Morrison jolted people out of self-satisfaction. So: a very dark psychedelia. The Doors released six albums; the last, L.A. Woman, hit No. 9 in 1971. Ironically it is seen as a comeback—ironic because in July 1971 Morrison died of heart failure in Paris, the third rock star after Jimi Hendrix and Janis Joplin to die.

The Doors to a degree stand for L.A. psychedelia, but they were not alone. We have mentioned Arthur Lee and Love several times; Love signed to Elektra before the Doors. They could have had Doors-level success, but Arthur Lee would not fly—so no touring. Without touring, your music stays local. In L.A. they were very successful; beside them the Doors looked small. The Doors were lucky to open for Love; Arthur Lee thought they were good and recommended them to Jac Holzman, and signed Elektra himself—then the Doors took off and Love stayed ordinary. They had a relatively hot single, “My Little Red Book,” No. 52 in 1966—we mentioned it with Pink Floyd. Their third album, 1967’s Forever Changes, rock critics have long called a great overlooked psychedelic album. You might hear Forever Changes and decide if it is a neglected classic.

Another West Coast band, Iron Butterfly, featured heavy rock; they were from San Diego. Their second album was most successful: In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida, summer 1968. The title track began as “In the Garden of Eden”; they turned it into “In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida.” In one Simpsons episode it is again “In the Garden of Eden”—search “Simpsons In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida” for that bit. (Note: in the episode Bart hands out the song in church as the hymn “In the Garden of Eden,” credited to Iron Butterfly.) Anyway the title track is 17 minutes; each member solos; it is heavy-riffed, the solos skilled, a bit psychedelic too.

Vanilla Fudge, from the East Coast, we call a “symphonic” psychedelia. They were good at turning a short song into a psychedelic rock journey; most famous is 1967’s “You Keep Me Hangin’ On,” which a year earlier was a two-minute Holland–Dozier–Holland hit for the Supremes. Vanilla Fudge stretched it to five minutes with sitar; I often have students hear the first minutes and guess where it goes—most cannot. That idea of expanding short songs into large psychedelic symphonies was their specialty. Their 1968 album The Beat Goes On was produced by Shadow Morton, tied to the Brill Building and girl groups. The band was not happy with it, but they used Sonny & Cher’s “The Beat Goes On” as a motif recurring through the album. Arranged songs run from the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries through the twentieth, including Beatles songs—a highly ambitious concept album. I think Vanilla Fudge’s adaptations contributed a lot to later progressive rock: the essence of turning short songs into long works.

Since we are in this period, talk about upstate New York and Bob Dylan. After his 1966 motorcycle accident Dylan withdrew to Woodstock, New York—you may not know where; a few hours north of New York City, suburban in feel, rural and plain. There he recorded with the Band. They were first the Hawks, named for Canadian singer Ronnie Hawkins; all but Levon Helm were Canadian. They had toured the world with Dylan in 1965–66; they already worked together. While Dylan hid at Woodstock they recorded much of what later became 1975’s The Basement Tapes. In that stretch two important records came out—one by Dylan, one by the Band—that not only defined the Americana movement but also mattered for country rock’s rise. Both 1968: Dylan’s John Wesley Harding hit No. 2 on the album chart; the Band’s Music from Big Pink only No. 30, but it is considered very influential.

That covers L.A. and elsewhere. Next time: festivals—meaning after psychedelic music went national in summer 1967, hippie culture swept the country; that is the chapter’s last section.
